examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Area Bounded Between a Curve and the Y-Axis by First Rewriting the Function
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013903/assets/eb7118486df97c3abae6c8492170090df0c654064799e04826a39a94bcfa22a8.png)

Find the area between the curve $y=\sqrt{x+1},$ the $y$-axis, and the lines $y=0$ and $y=1,$ as shown above.
examples.worked_solution:
First, we make $x$ the subject:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt{x+1} \\ {y}^{2} & =x+1 \\ x & ={y}^{2}-1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{2}-1)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}-y{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =(\frac{1}{3}-0)-(1-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}-1 \\  & =-\frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We obtained a negative number because the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis. So the area that we want is $\left|-\dfrac{2}{3}\right| = \dfrac{2}{3}.$

feedback.problem: Find the area of the finite region bounded between the curve $x=2{y}^{2}-2$ and the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the $y$-intercepts of the curve:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{y}^{2}-2 & =0 \\ 2{y}^{2} & =2 \\ {y}^{2} & =1 \\ y & =\pm 1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we draw a sketch of the region:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14013903/assets/a2156d559a715d668f064c91132719d2678ab4af66bf83591fa5687d6e23d95e.png)

We want to find the area between the curve $x=2{y}^{2}-2$ and the $y$-axis from $y=-1$ to $y=1.$ 
To find the area, we compute the corresponding definite integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & ={\int }_{c}^{d}x(y)\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}(2{y}^{2}-2)\,\text{d}y \\  & =2{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{y}^{2}-2)\,\text{d}y \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{1}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y-4{\int }_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}y \\  & =4\cdot {\frac{{y}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{1}-4\cdot y{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =4(\frac{1}{3}-0)-4(1-0) \\  & =\frac{4}{3}-4 \\  & =-\frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We obtained a negative number because the region lies to the left of the $y$-axis. So the area that we want is $|-\frac{8}{3}|=\frac{8}{3}.$
